rak.name: Rakı
rak.summary: An anise-flavored, twice-distilled Turkish spirit and national drink of Turkey, at least 40% alcohol and often served with seafood or meze.

vitis-vinifera.name: Vitis vinifera
vitis-vinifera.summary: Species of grape vine native to the Mediterranean, Central Europe and southwest Asia; nearly all major wine grape varieties belong to this species.

european-anchovy.name: European anchovy
european-anchovy.summary: A small forage fish related to the herring, found along the coasts of Europe and Africa, including the Mediterranean, Black Sea and Sea of Azov, and widely fished by humans.

urfa.name: Urfa
urfa.summary: A city in southeastern Turkey nicknamed the City of Prophets for its ties to Jewish, Christian and Islamic history, near the ancient site of Göbekli Tepe.

gaziantep.name: Gaziantep
gaziantep.summary: A major city in south-central Turkey, historically called Aintab, today famous for kebabs and desserts such as baklava and künefe.

ad-yaman.name: Adıyaman
ad-yaman.summary: City in southeastern Turkey with a mostly Kurdish population, serving as the administrative center of Adıyaman Province.

adana.name: Adana
adana.summary: A large city in southern Turkey on the Seyhan River, at the heart of the Cilicia region, historically important for its mountain pass, trade routes, and metal and agricultural wealth.

mustafa-kemal-atat-rk.name: Mustafa Kemal Atatürk
mustafa-kemal-atat-rk.summary: Turkish field marshal and statesman (1881-1938) who founded the Republic of Turkey, served as its first president, and led sweeping reforms known as Kemalism.

tekirda.name: Tekirdağ
tekirda.summary: A city on Turkey's Sea of Marmara coast, a commercial harbour town best known for its rakı, cherries, and agricultural trade.

thrace.name: Thrace
thrace.summary: A historical and geographical region in Southeast Europe, roughly matching the Roman province of Thrace, spanning parts of modern Bulgaria, Greece and Turkey.

alafranga-and-alaturca.name: Alafranga
alafranga-and-alaturca.summary: A term for Western-style culture in the late Ottoman Empire and Turkey, contrasted with alaturca, the traditional Turkish style.

ark-y.name: Şarköy
ark-y.summary: A seaside town and district of Tekirdağ Province, Turkey, on the north coast of the Sea of Marmara in East Thrace.

elaz.name: Elazığ
elaz.summary: A city in eastern Turkey's Anatolia region, built near the former city of Harput in the upper Euphrates valley, with a population of about 387,000.

ekerpare.name: Şekerpare
ekerpare.summary: A Turkish dessert of semolina cookies topped with nuts and soaked in sugar syrup, especially popular during Ramadan, and also enjoyed in Egypt and the Levant as 'lady's eyelashes.'

kalecik-karas.name: Kalecik Karası
kalecik-karas.summary: A Turkish grape variety and wine named after the Kalecik district of Ankara Province, prized for its distinctive taste and winner of several international wine awards.

first-national-architectural-movement.name: First National Architectural Movement
first-national-architectural-movement.summary: A Turkish architectural style prevalent from 1908 to the 1930s that revived Ottoman and Anatolian Seljuk elements in modern buildings, led by architects such as Vedat Tek and Ahmet Kemaleddin.

vedat-tek.name: Vedat Tek
vedat-tek.summary: A Turkish architect (1873–1942), the last court architect of the Ottoman Empire and a leading figure of the First Turkish National Architectural Movement.

mimar-kemaleddin.name: Mimar Kemaleddin
mimar-kemaleddin.summary: A Turkish architect (1870–1927), one of the leading figures of the First National architectural movement, alongside Vedat Tek.

grand-post-office.name: Istanbul Grand Post Office
grand-post-office.summary: Office building in Istanbul's Sirkeci neighborhood, designed by Vedat Tek and built between 1905 and 1909. It is Turkey's largest post office building and has housed a postal museum since 2000.

bebek-mosque.name: Bebek Mosque
bebek-mosque.summary: Mosque in Istanbul's Bebek neighborhood on the Bosphorus, designed by Mimar Kemaleddin. It was built in 1913 on the site of an earlier mosque commissioned by Grand Vizier Nevşehirli Damat Ibrahim Pasha.

sirkeci.name: Sirkeci
sirkeci.summary: A neighborhood in Istanbul's Fatih district, known in Byzantine times as Prosphorion, home to the Sirkeci railway station, terminus of the Orient Express.

young-turks.name: Young Turks
young-turks.summary: A broad opposition movement against Sultan Abdul Hamid II's absolutist rule, whose Committee of Union and Progress prevailed in the 1908 revolution.

committee-of-union-and-progress.name: Committee of Union and Progress
committee-of-union-and-progress.summary: An Ottoman revolutionary group, secret society and political party active from 1889 to 1926, associated with the 'Young Turks', that forced restoration of the 1876 constitution in 1908.

war-of-independence-museum.name: War of Independence Museum
war-of-independence-museum.summary: A museum in Ankara, housed in the first Turkish Grand National Assembly building, displaying photographs, documents and furniture from the Turkish War of Independence.

mimar-sinan-fine-arts-university.name: Academy of Fine Arts in Istanbul
mimar-sinan-fine-arts-university.summary: A public art university in Istanbul's Fındıklı district (now Mimar Sinan Fine Arts University), established in 1882 under Osman Hamdi Bey.

septimius-severus.name: Septimius Severus
septimius-severus.summary: Septimius Severus: Roman emperor from 193 to 211, born in Leptis Magna in the Roman province of Africa, who defeated rival claimants, sacked the Parthian capital Ctesiphon, and expanded Rome's eastern and African frontiers.

ny-carlsberg-glyptotek.name: Ny Carlsberg Glyptotek
ny-carlsberg-glyptotek.summary: An art museum in Copenhagen built from the private collection of Carl Jacobsen (1842–1914), son of the Carlsberg Breweries founder, noted for ancient Mediterranean sculpture and French Impressionist paintings.

bubon-lycia.name: Bubon (Boubon)
bubon-lycia.summary: Ancient city of Lycia, in what is now Turkey, that formed part of the Cabalia district along with Balbura and Oenoanda.

burdur.name: Burdur
burdur.summary: City in southwestern Turkey on the shore of Lake Burdur, seat of Burdur Province.

crowne-plaza-istanbul-old-city.name: Tayyare Apartments
crowne-plaza-istanbul-old-city.summary: A complex of four buildings in Istanbul, designed by architect Mimar Kemaleddin and completed in 1922, built as public housing for victims of a major fire before later becoming a hotel.

occupation-of-constantinople.name: Allied occupation of Constantinople
occupation-of-constantinople.summary: The 1918–1923 occupation of the Ottoman capital by British, French, Italian and Greek forces after World War I, ending with the Treaty of Lausanne and helping spur the Turkish War of Independence.

sultanahmet-jail.name: Sultanahmet Jail
sultanahmet-jail.summary: Former prison in Istanbul, now the luxury Four Seasons Hotel at Sultanahmet, on the city's historical peninsula.

mihran-azaryan.name: Mihran Azaryan
mihran-azaryan.summary: An Ottoman Armenian and Turkish architect (1876–1952) best known for designing Istanbul's Büyükada Pier.

haydarpa-a.name: Haydarpaşa
haydarpa-a.summary: A locality on the Asian side of Istanbul, named after Ottoman Vizier Haydar Pasha, known for public buildings including its terminal and port.

turkish-national-movement.name: Turkish National Movement
turkish-national-movement.summary: The Turkish revolutionaries' political and military movement, largely made up of former Committee of Union and Progress members, that founded the modern Republic of Turkey after the Ottoman Empire's WWI defeat and partition.

enver-pasha.name: Enver Pasha
enver-pasha.summary: Ottoman military officer and revolutionary (1881–1922) who served as Minister of War from 1914 to 1918 and was one of the Three Pashas ruling during World War I.

battle-of-sarikamish.name: Battle of Sarikamish
battle-of-sarikamish.summary: A World War I battle (1914 to 1915) in which Russian forces decisively defeated an ill-equipped Ottoman army in harsh winter conditions, with about 25,000 Ottoman soldiers freezing to death before the main fighting.

batumi.name: Batumi
batumi.summary: Georgia's second-largest city, on the Black Sea coast near the Turkish border; formerly known as Batum, it was ceded by Bolshevik Russia in the 1918 Treaty of Brest-Litovsk.

kars.name: Kars
kars.summary: A city in northeast Turkey that was capital of the Bagratid kingdom of Armenia from 929 to 961 and had an Armenian ethnic majority until 1920.

treaty-of-brest-litovsk.name: Treaty of Brest-Litovsk
treaty-of-brest-litovsk.summary: A March 1918 peace treaty in which Bolshevik Russia withdrew from World War I, ceding vast territory to the Central Powers and recognizing Finland's independence.

smyrna.name: Smyrna
smyrna.summary: An ancient Greek city on the Aegean coast of Anatolia, renamed İzmir in 1930, with remains from the Archaic and Roman periods still found within the modern city.

armistice-of-mudros.name: Armistice of Mudros
armistice-of-mudros.summary: Agreement signed on 30 October 1918 ending hostilities between the Ottoman Empire and the Allies in the Middle Eastern theatre of World War I, leading to Allied occupation and the partition of Ottoman territory.

treaty-of-s-vres.name: Treaty of Sèvres
treaty-of-s-vres.summary: Unratified 1920 treaty that would have required the Ottoman Empire to cede large territories to the Allies, later superseded by the Treaty of Lausanne.

treaty-of-lausanne.name: Treaty of Lausanne
treaty-of-lausanne.summary: Signed in July 1923 after the failed Treaty of Sèvres, it also declared an amnesty for wartime crimes committed between 1914 and 1922, including the Armenian and Greek genocides.

battle-of-k-tahya-eski-ehir.name: Battle of Kütahya-Eskişehir
battle-of-k-tahya-eski-ehir.summary: 1921 battle in which Greek forces defeated Turkish troops during the Greek-Turkish war but failed to encircle them, a strategic misstep later reversed at Sakarya.

battle-of-the-sakarya.name: Battle of the Sakarya
battle-of-the-sakarya.summary: A 21-day battle in August and September 1921 near the Sakarya River that halted the Greek advance on Ankara and became the turning point of the Turkish War of Independence.

republic-of-aras.name: Republic of Aras
republic-of-aras.summary: A short-lived, unrecognized state in the South Caucasus declared in December 1918 with Ottoman and Azerbaijani backing, ended when Armenian troops took control in mid-1919.

south-ossetia.name: South Ossetia
south-ossetia.summary: A partially recognized state in the South Caucasus of about 56,500 people, claimed by Georgia but under heavy Russian military and political influence since a 2008 war.

abkhazia.name: Abkhazia
abkhazia.summary: Partially recognised state on the Black Sea coast in the South Caucasus, considered by most countries part of Georgia; it gained de facto independence after a 1992–1993 war.

viktor-yushchenko.name: Viktor Yushchenko
viktor-yushchenko.summary: Ukraine's third president, from 2005 to 2010, who survived a dioxin poisoning during the disputed 2004 election that sparked the Orange Revolution and led to his eventual win in a repeat vote.

sevastopol.name: Sevastopol
sevastopol.summary: The largest city in Crimea and a major Black Sea port, founded by Catherine the Great in 1783 as a base for Russia's Black Sea Fleet; internationally recognized as Ukrainian but occupied by Russia since 2014.

n-z-m-hikmet.name: Nâzım Hikmet
n-z-m-hikmet.summary: A Turkish poet, playwright and novelist (1902–1963) celebrated for his lyrical style; a 'romantic communist' repeatedly jailed or exiled for his politics, with poetry translated into over 50 languages.

faz-l-h-sn-da-larca.name: Fazıl Hüsnü Dağlarca
faz-l-h-sn-da-larca.summary: A prolific Turkish poet (1914–2008) who published more than 60 poetry collections and won the Struga Poetry Evenings Golden Wreath Award.

beh-et-necatigil.name: Behçet Necatigil
beh-et-necatigil.summary: Turkish poet, teacher and translator (1916-1979), regarded as one of modern Turkish poetry's most important figures and known as the "Poet of Houses."

turgut-uyar.name: Turgut Uyar
turgut-uyar.summary: A Turkish poet who lived from 1927 to 1985.

edip-cansever.name: Edip Cansever
edip-cansever.summary: A Turkish poet (1928-1986) of the Second New movement, described as influenced by surrealism and as a nonconformist.

cemal-s-reya.name: Cemal Süreya
cemal-s-reya.summary: A Kurdish Turkish poet, writer and translator (1931–1990), a pioneer of Turkey's modernist İkinci Yeni poetry movement and a translator of nearly forty French books.

ece-ayhan.name: Ece Ayhan
ece-ayhan.summary: Turkish poet (1931 to 2002) and a leading figure of the Second New literary movement, known for works such as Blind Cat Black featuring homoerotic poetry.

sezai-karako.name: Sezai Karakoç
sezai-karako.summary: Turkish writer, thinker, community leader and poet who lived from 1933 to 2021.

can-y-cel.name: Can Yücel
can-y-cel.summary: A Turkish poet, 1926 to 1999, known for writing in colloquial, everyday language.

i-smet-zel.name: İsmet Özel
i-smet-zel.summary: A Turkish poet and writer born in 1944 in Kayseri.

hasan-h-seyin-korkmazgil.name: Hasan Hüseyin Korkmazgil
hasan-h-seyin-korkmazgil.summary: Leading Turkish socialist realist poet (1927–1984), born in Gürün, Sivas Province.

farewell-anatolia.name: Farewell Anatolia
farewell-anatolia.summary: A 1962 historical novel by Dido Sotiriou following a Greek peasant through the collapse of the Greek front in the Greco-Turkish War, one of the best-known Greek novels of its era.

dido-sotiriou.name: Dido Sotiriou
dido-sotiriou.summary: Greek novelist, journalist and playwright, 1909 to 2004.

aziz-sancar.name: Aziz Sancar
aziz-sancar.summary: Turkish-American molecular biologist, born 1946, who won the 2015 Nobel Prize in Chemistry for explaining how cells repair damaged DNA.

mardin-province.name: Mardin Province
mardin-province.summary: A province and metropolitan municipality in southeastern Turkey with about 870,000 people, whose capital city Mardin is its second-largest city.

tomas-lindahl.name: Tomas Lindahl
tomas-lindahl.summary: Swedish-British scientist who won the 2015 Nobel Prize in Chemistry, shared with Paul Modrich and Aziz Sancar, for studies of DNA repair.

paul-l-modrich.name: Paul L. Modrich
paul-l-modrich.summary: American biochemist at Duke University who won the 2015 Nobel Prize in Chemistry, shared with Aziz Sancar and Tomas Lindahl, for research on DNA mismatch repair.

orhan-pamuk.name: Orhan Pamuk
orhan-pamuk.summary: Turkish novelist and winner of the 2006 Nobel Prize in Literature, the first Turkish Nobel laureate, known for novels including My Name Is Red and Snow.

scientific-and-technological-research-co.name: TÜBİTAK
scientific-and-technological-research-co.summary: Turkey's national science and technology agency, set up to shape research policy, fund development, and advise the government as secretariat of its top science policymaking body.
scientific-and-technological-research-co.source_title: Scientific and Technological Research Council of Turkey

cahit-arf.name: Cahit Arf
cahit-arf.summary: A Turkish mathematician (1910 to 1997) known for the Arf invariant in topology and the Hasse–Arf theorem in ramification theory.

erdal-i-n-n.name: Erdal İnönü
erdal-i-n-n.summary: Turkish theoretical physicist and politician (1926–2007) who served as interim prime minister in 1993 and led two social democratic parties; son of Turkey's second president, İsmet İnönü.

feza-g-rsey.name: Feza Gürsey
feza-g-rsey.summary: A Turkish mathematician and physicist (1921-1992) known for work on the chiral model and SU(6) symmetry in particle physics.

savur.name: Savur
savur.summary: A municipality and district of Mardin Province in Turkey, with a population of about 24,800, whose name means 'mountain ridge' in Syriac.

atat-rk-university.name: Atatürk University
atat-rk-university.summary: Public research university founded in 1957 in Erzurum, Turkey, in collaboration with the University of Nebraska, and a center of education for eastern Turkey.

erzurum.name: Erzurum
erzurum.summary: A city in eastern Turkey over 1,900 meters above sea level, built on the site of the ancient city of Theodosiopolis.

bilkent-university.name: Bilkent University
bilkent-university.summary: A private, non-profit research university in Ankara, Turkey, founded in 1984 by İhsan Doğramacı as the country's first non-profit private university.

i-hsan-do-ramac.name: İhsan Doğramacı
i-hsan-do-ramac.summary: A Turkish pediatrician and educator (1915–2010) who founded Bilkent University and Hacettepe University, chaired UNICEF's executive board, and became founding president of Turkey's Council of Higher Education.

erdal-ar-kan.name: Erdal Arıkan
erdal-ar-kan.summary: Turkish electrical engineering professor at Bilkent University, born 1958, known for inventing polar codes, a coding technique that became a key component of 5G technology.

polar-code-coding-theory.name: Polar codes
polar-code-coding-theory.summary: An error-correcting coding technique, invented by Erdal Arıkan, that was the first to provably achieve channel capacity and later became a key part of 5G mobile technology.

tai-tf-kaan.name: TAI Kaan
tai-tf-kaan.summary: A fifth-generation stealth fighter jet developed by Turkish Aerospace Industries to replace the Turkish Air Force's F-16s, with its prototype completing a maiden flight in February 2024.

m-rted-airfield-command.name: Mürted Airfield
m-rted-airfield-command.summary: A Turkish Air Force base near Ankara that was used by pro-coup forces during the failed 2016 coup attempt and was later renamed back to its historic name, Mürted.

mustafa-subhi.name: Mustafa Subhi
mustafa-subhi.summary: Turkish revolutionary and communist active during the dissolution of the Ottoman Empire, who lived from 1883 to 1921.

turkish-war-of-independence.name: Turkish War of Independence
turkish-war-of-independence.summary: A 1919–1923 series of campaigns and a revolution led by the Turkish National Movement against Allied and separatist forces, ending Ottoman rule and establishing the Republic of Turkey under Mustafa Kemal Atatürk.

trabzon.name: Trabzon
trabzon.summary: City on Turkey's Black Sea coast, founded in 756 BC by Greek colonists, later capital of the Byzantine successor Empire of Trebizond before falling to the Ottomans in 1461.

talaat-pasha.name: Talat Pasha
talaat-pasha.summary: Ottoman politician who served as de facto leader of the Empire from 1913 to 1918 and Grand Vizier during World War I; convicted as a war criminal and called the architect of the Armenian genocide.

ardahan.name: Ardahan
ardahan.summary: A city in northeastern Turkey near the Georgian border, ceded by the Ottomans to Russia along with Batum and Kars under the 1918 Treaty of Brest-Litovsk.

tbilisi.name: Tbilisi
tbilisi.summary: Capital of Georgia, founded in the 5th century CE by Vakhtang I of Iberia on the Kura River; known as Tiflis while part of the Russian Empire from 1801 to 1917.

first-republic-of-armenia.name: First Republic of Armenia
first-republic-of-armenia.summary: Independent Armenian state that existed from 1918 to 1920 in former Russian Armenia, the first Armenian state since the Middle Ages.

battle-of-sardarabad.name: Battle of Sardarabad
battle-of-sardarabad.summary: A 1918 battle near Yerevan in which Armenian troops halted an invading Ottoman army, preventing the destruction of the Armenian nation and paving the way for the First Republic of Armenia.

treaty-of-batum.name: Treaty of Batum
treaty-of-batum.summary: A June 1918 treaty between the Ottoman Empire and the new republics of Armenia, Azerbaijan and Georgia; it was the first treaty signed by the Armenian and Azerbaijani states.

ottoman-dynasty.name: Ottoman dynasty
ottoman-dynasty.summary: The imperial House of Osman, tracing to Osman I in northwestern Anatolia around 1299, which ruled the Ottoman Empire until the sultanate was abolished in 1922.

osmano-lu-family.name: Osmanoğlu family
osmano-lu-family.summary: The historical House of Osman, the Ottoman ruling dynasty from about 1299 to 1922; its descendants took the surname Osmanoğlu after being exiled in 1924.

abd-lmecid-ii.name: Abdülmecid II
abd-lmecid-ii.summary: Abdülmecid II: Last Ottoman caliph and the only one ever elected by Turkey's parliament, also known as an artist interested in literature, painting and music.

grand-national-assembly-of-turkey.name: Grand National Assembly
grand-national-assembly-of-turkey.summary: Turkey's unicameral legislative body, the sole institution granted legislative power under the country's constitution.

yeni-d-nya.name: Yeni Dünya
yeni-d-nya.summary: A communist journal published in Soviet Russia and Transcaucasia from 1918 to 1921, founded and edited by Mustafa Subhi, that helped gather the first generation of Turkish communists.

osman-i.name: Osman I
osman-i.summary: Eponymous founder of the Ottoman Empire, who died in 1323 or 1324; almost nothing factual survives about him since no written sources date from his lifetime.

dirili-ertu-rul.name: Diriliş: Ertuğrul
dirili-ertu-rul.summary: Turkish historical drama series created by Mehmet Bozdağ, inspired by the life of Ertuğrul Bey, father of Osman I. It follows his leadership of the Kayı tribe in 13th-century Anatolia and was also streamed on Netflix.

kurulu-osman.name: Kuruluş: Osman
kurulu-osman.summary: Turkish historical television series produced by Mehmet Bozdağ, which premiered on ATV in 2019. It follows Osman's struggle to found an independent beylik and continues Diriliş: Ertuğrul.

syed-ameer-ali.name: Syed Ameer Ali
syed-ameer-ali.summary: Indian jurist and political leader (1849–1928) who wrote influential books on Muslim history and Islam. He helped found the All India Muslim League and backed separate electorates for Muslims and the Khilafat Movement.

franz-babinger.name: Franz Babinger
franz-babinger.summary: German orientalist and historian of the Ottoman Empire (1891-1967), best known for his biography of the Ottoman sultan Mehmed II, "the Conqueror".
